keyVerseText: For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.
rootMeaning: The word μεγαλεῖος (megaleîos) is derived from the root μέγας (mégas), which conveys the idea of greatness in size, strength, or intensity. This root implies not just physical largeness but also a sense of exalted magnitude or power. Thus, μεγαλεῖος carries the sense of something magnificent or splendid, highlighting an extraordinary and conspicuous quality beyond ordinary greatness. This etymological foundation enriches the English gloss by emphasizing not only size but also a majestic or awe-inspiring character.
usageInScripture: Megaleîos appears only twice in the New Testament, where it is translated primarily as 'great things' or 'the wonderful works.' This limited but consistent usage underscores its role in describing acts or deeds that are remarkable and divinely significant. The word's application to mighty works suggests a focus on God's powerful and awe-inspiring actions, reflecting both objective greatness and subjective perfection. Its rarity in Scripture highlights its special emphasis on the grandeur of God's deeds.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding μεγαλεῖος as denoting magnificent and splendid works helps believers appreciate the magnitude of God's actions in history and salvation. It points to the divine power and holiness that characterize God's interventions, reminding Christians that God’s works are not only great in scale but also perfect in purpose. This term elevates our view of God's providence and grace, encouraging faith in His sovereign ability to accomplish mighty and wonderful things. It also invites worship that recognizes God's majestic nature and the holiness of His name.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 1:49, the phrase 'he that is mighty hath done to me great things' uses μεγαλεῖος to highlight the extraordinary nature of God's deeds. The word stresses that these works are not merely large but splendid and awe-inspiring, underscoring God's power and faithfulness. This magnifies the holiness of His name and invites believers to trust in God's magnificent providence and grace, as revealed in His mighty acts toward His people.
